claims.reason: The proofs of `Integrable.essSup_smul` and `Integrable.smul_essSup` are mirror-image copies. Each has three steps. (a) Rewrite to `MemLp 1`. (b) Convert `essSup (‖g ·‖ₑ) μ ≠ ∞` to `eLpNorm g ∞ μ ≠ ∞` via `eLpNorm_exponent_top`. (c) Run a Hölder `calc` with `eLpNorm_smul_le_mul_eLpNorm_of_pos` (p, q = ∞, 1 and 1, ∞) and `ENNReal.mul_lt_top`. This is the same Hölder step that `Integrable.smul_of_top_right` and `Integrable.smul_of_top_left` (lines 981 and 991) already get from `MemLp.smul`, with the same exponents. The hypotheses match. `smul_of_top_right` needs `[NormedRing 𝕜] [Module 𝕜 β] [IsBoundedSMul 𝕜 β]`, the same as `essSup_smul`. `MemLp.smul` in `CompareExp.lean` only needs `[MulActionWithZero 𝕜 E]`, so `smul_of_top_left` can be relaxed from `Module` to `MulActionWithZero`, which preserves the generality of `smul_essSup`. The goals `fun x => g x • f x` and `g • f` are definitionally equal, so `exact` should work. `essSup_smul` is used in `Haar/Quotient.lean` (lines 415 and 457). Its statement does not change, so those uses are unaffected. Two caveats. The new helper is a one-line lemma, so the gain is mostly removing the duplicated Hölder `calc` and the `simpa using!` instance step. The two `smul_of_top_*` lemmas must be moved before line 575, or the `essSup` lemmas moved after them. There is no dependency cycle, because the `smul_of_top_*` proofs use only `MemLp.smul`.

theorem Integrable.smul_of_top_right {f : α → β} {φ : α → 𝕜} (hf : Integrable f μ)
    (hφ : MemLp φ ∞ μ) : Integrable (φ • f) μ := by
  rw [← memLp_one_iff_integrable] at hf ⊢
  exact MemLp.smul hφ hf

theorem MemLp.smul {p q r : ℝ≥0∞} {f : α → E} {φ : α → 𝕜} (hφ : MemLp φ p μ) (hf : MemLp f q μ)
    [hpqr : HolderTriple p q r] : MemLp (φ • f) r μ

That is routine rewriting, not nontrivial mathematical machinery. The closing steps also differ: `simp_rw [NNReal.smul_def, ENNReal.toReal]` against `congr!`. The `coe_smul₀` proof is not a second copy of this reduction. It builds on the non-₀ lemma by replacing `f` with `hf.mk f`. The proposed move is also incomplete. `smul₀'` depends on `coe_smul₀`, which sits after `smul'`, so that lemma would have to move too. Specialising a more general lemma is a different cleanup (redundant or special-case lemmas). It does not meet the repeated-proof-machinery threshold.
